add-subtract-20: add two numbers within 20 in my head using strategies such as making a ten, doubles, and doubles plus one.
subtract within 20 in my head by thinking addition, counting back, or going back through ten.
use an addition fact to find related addition and subtraction facts in the same fact family.
find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation within 20 and tell if an equation is true.
odd-even-arrays: tell whether a group of up to 20 objects is odd or even by making pairs or counting by 2s.
write an even number as the sum of two equal addends, such as 14 = 7 + 7.
find the total in an array with up to 5 rows and 5 columns and write an addition equation with equal addends.
solve word problems about objects in rows and columns by drawing an array and writing an equation.
place-value-1000: explain that 100 is the same as ten tens and trade between tens and hundreds.
tell how many hundreds, tens, and ones are in a three-digit number and the value of each digit.
tell that 100, 200, … 900 are one to nine hundreds with 0 tens and 0 ones.
read and write numbers to 1,000 as numerals, in words, and in expanded form.
count-compare-1000: count forward and backward within 1,000, including across tens and hundreds.
skip count by 5s, 10s, and 100s from any starting number and continue the pattern.
compare two three-digit numbers using hundreds, tens, and ones and record it with >, =, or <.
mentally add or subtract 10 or 100 to a number from 100 to 900.
add-subtract-100: add two-digit numbers within 100 using place value, and make a new ten when the ones add to 10 or more.
subtract within 100 using place value, breaking apart a ten when there are not enough ones.
use addition to check subtraction and to find an unknown number within 100.
add up to four two-digit numbers by adding tens and ones or by finding friendly pairs.
explain why a strategy works using place value and properties of operations.
word-problems-100: solve add-to and take-from problems when the result, the change, or the start is unknown.
solve put-together and take-apart problems when the total or one part is unknown.
solve compare problems that ask how many more or how many fewer, or the bigger or smaller amount.
solve two-step word problems within 100 and write an equation with a symbol for the unknown.
add-subtract-1000: add three-digit numbers with base-ten blocks or drawings by adding hundreds, tens, and ones.
add within 1,000 when I need to make a new ten or a new hundred and relate it to a written method.
subtract three-digit numbers with base-ten blocks or drawings, or by counting up.
subtract within 1,000 when I need to break apart a ten or a hundred, including across zeros.
measuring-length: measure the length of an object to the nearest inch or centimeter with a ruler.
choose a ruler, yardstick, meter stick, or measuring tape and the best unit for the length I need to measure.
measure an object with two units and explain why a smaller unit gives a bigger number.
estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters, and meters using benchmarks.
measure two objects and find how much longer one is than the other.
measure several objects to the nearest whole unit and show the data on a line plot.
length-number-line: solve addition and subtraction word problems about lengths in the same unit.
show a whole number as a length from 0 on a number line with equally spaced numbers.
show sums and differences within 100 as jumps on a number line.
time-money: tell and write time to the nearest five minutes from analog and digital clocks.
use AM and PM (a.m. and p.m.) to tell the time of day for events.
find the value of a group of quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies and write it with ¢.
find the value of dollar bills and coins together and write it with $ and ¢.
solve word problems about money, including finding totals, change, and how much more is needed.
graphs-data: read a picture graph where each picture stands for 1 and tell how many are in each category.
read a bar graph with a scale of 1 and tell how many are in each category.
use a picture graph or bar graph to solve put-together, take-apart, and compare problems.
make a picture graph or bar graph from a tally chart or table with up to four categories.
shapes-equal-shares: identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, and hexagons by counting their sides and angles.
draw or choose a shape that has a given number of sides, angles, or vertices.
identify a cube and describe its 6 equal square faces, edges, and vertices.
partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find how many.
partition circles and rectangles into 2, 3, or 4 equal shares and describe them as halves, thirds, or fourths.
describe a whole as two halves, three thirds, or four fourths, and explain that equal shares can have different shapes.
